claims.text: Atomically dispersed Pt on a CeO2-based support will enhance catalytic activity relative to conventional Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomically dispersed Pt on CeO2 will enhance catalyst durability relative to conventional Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Replacing Pt nanoparticles with single-atom Pt sites will reduce overall platinum-group-metal consumption.
Single-atom Pt sites can be anchored on CeO2.
Single-atom Pt sites on CeO2 form stronger metal-support interactions than conventional Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Using CeO2 with atomically dispersed Pt enhances oxygen-storage capacity.
Strong metal-support interactions limit Pt sintering and aggregation.
Strong Pt-O-Ce bonding in the single-atom configuration increases the availability of active sites.
Strong Pt-O-Ce bonding improves oxygen activation.
The single-atom configuration stabilizes Pt at high temperatures and maintains its dispersion.
Atomically dispersed Pt on CeO2 will maintain or improve CO conversion relative to Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomically dispersed Pt on CeO2 will maintain or improve NOx conversion relative to Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomically dispersed Pt on CeO2 will maintain or improve hydrocarbon conversion relative to Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomically dispersed Pt on CeO2 will retain greater performance over thermal cycling than conventional Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
The predicted activity and durability can be achieved with approximately 20-30% less Pt.
The predicted benefits should persist under fluctuating oxygen levels and temperatures up to approximately 800 degrees Celsius.
The predicted benefits apply in both stoichiometric and oxygen-rich exhaust regimes.
Exposure above approximately 800 degrees Celsius may limit the predicted benefits.
Inadequate control of the thermal stability of the single-atom dispersion may limit the predicted benefits.
